# requires: store
#
# The issuer asking for the lease back. Ours expired and none could be revoked
# early with a reason the holder could act on, which is the half WDDM and
# Android both have and this design lacked: the residency broker could name a
# model loaded twice and never evict either copy.
#
# A recall is addressed to one holding, so it presents the epoch the issuer
# read, not one it holds: step 3 names an owner that never claimed and is
# refused as stale, step 4 names the holder and no reason and is refused as
# invalid. Step 5 lands: the reason is on the record, the intent is untouched,
# the record declares the model, and the lease now ends at the deadline.
#
# What the holder may still do is the part a second implementer has to be
# told. It may renew (6) and it may checkpoint (8), because winding down takes
# time and a holder that cannot record what it proved on the way out loses it.
# It may not shed the recall by re-claiming (7). And the renew at 6 asked for
# five seconds and got the deadline, which is only visible when the deadline
# passes: step 10 is refused, and without the cap it would have landed.
#
# Step 10 is the fallback. Nothing killed anything; the lease lapsed and the
# holder's next write was refused exactly as a lapsed write always is. The
# record still says who was asked and what they proved (12), and the job is
# offered to a sweep (11). A claim starts a new holding with no recall on it
# (13). Steps 14 to 16 are compliance: a holder that releases under recall
# leaves a pending record that still says it was asked, which is the
# difference between "nobody renewed" and "somebody was asked to stop" that
# a later reader needs — and nobody holds it, so it cannot be recalled again.
# Step 19: a finished job has nothing to give back.
submit A size=64 digest=good src=file
claim A alpha 5000
recall A beta 800 yield
recall A alpha 800
recall A alpha 800 yield
renew A alpha 5000
claim A alpha 5000
progress A alpha 8 {"verified_prefix":8}
sleep 1000
progress A alpha 16 {"verified_prefix":16}
orphans
state A
claim A beta 5000
recall A beta 5000 make room
release A beta
recall A beta 500 yield
claim A gamma 5000
finish A gamma complete
recall A gamma 500 yield

# expect 3: stale-epoch [JOB-R1]
# expect 3: recall=none
# expect 4: invalid [JOB-R2]
# expect 5: ok [JOB-R3]
# expect 5: recall=yield
# expect 5: held=yes
# expect 5: want=run [JOB-R8]
# expect 5: content=abstraction.job/base@1,abstraction.job/recall@1 [JOB-D9]
# expect 5: crit=abstraction.job/base@1,abstraction.job/recall@1 [JOB-D9]
# expect 6: ok
# expect 7: lease-held [JOB-R5]
# expect 8: ok
# expect 8: done=8
# expect 10: lease-expired [JOB-R4]
# expect 10: done=8 [JOB-R3]
# expect 10: held=no
# expect 11: ok A [JOB-R6]
# expect 12: recall=yield
# expect 12: state=running
# expect 12: epoch=1
# expect 13: ok [JOB-R7]
# expect 13: epoch=2
# expect 13: recall=none
# expect 13: content=abstraction.job/base@1
# expect 14: ok
# expect 15: ok [JOB-R6]
# expect 15: state=pending
# expect 15: held=no
# expect 15: recall=make room
# expect 16: lease-expired [JOB-R2]
# expect 19: terminal [JOB-R2]
